source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
NTT VA5 publishes 32 MW of IT capacity. Across the 19 Virginia facilities on this site that have published a megawatt figure, the total is 1,326 MW, and VA5 ranks 13th by that measure, accounting for roughly 2.4 percent of that published total. Virginia has 326 facilities mapped in OpenStreetMap, and most of them publish no capacity figure, so the 1,326 MW total understates the state's true footprint by an unknown amount.

At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 32 MW of IT load is roughly 800 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a conventional enterprise density, the same 32 MW supports roughly 3,200 racks. The operator publishes no rack count, no cooling architecture, and no power-usage-effectiveness figure, so which end of that range applies is not determinable from published data. The address, Megawatt Drive, is shared with several neighboring campuses, placing VA5 inside the Ashburn corridor where power delivery and fiber density are well established, but interconnection capacity and utility allocation for this specific building are not published.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications this site retrieved, so no statement can be made about what compliance regimes the campus formally qualifies for. VA5 is a mid-tier asset by published megawatts within a state that leads US data center concentration, meaning its 32 MW sits in a market where much larger neighbors compete for the same power allocation and tenant demand. Whether 32 MW represents the campus's full buildout or a phase of a larger project is not published.
